newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos swims to dispel illness rumours.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos swims to dispel illness rumours.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos swam six laps at the presidential palace pool on Wednesday in an apparent effort to dispel rumours of his ill health.
Clad in blue trunks, Ramos swam from side to side of the 25-metre (80-foot) pool with slow, measured strokes and then told reporters he could have done 20 laps but he did not have time.
"The six laps (are) just really a warming up session for me," he told his weekly news conference after the swim.

Rumours that Ramos, who turns 69 next month, collapsed while at work on Tuesday prompted a flurry of official denials but the disclaimers failed to settle the stock market, which fell nearly 19 points, or 0.56 percent, to 3,339.83 points on Wednesday.
Apparently to ease the market, Ramos took to the pool after trading closed and left four cabinet ministers and five other aides puffing in his wake during the swim.

Ramos's health has become a major public concern since he underwent surgery on December 23 for the removal of a cholesterol lump in a vein in his neck. His doctors said the operation saved him from a possible stroke.
Ramos, a workaholic who used to work 16 to 18 hours a day before the operation, has slightly scaled down his activities but still maintains a full schedule.
He has resumed his provincial trips and is to visit Qatar, Bahrain, India, Pakistan and Bangladesh in a 10-day foreign trip from March 2 to 10.
"I don't know how these rumours begin and how they persist," Ramos said. "But as you may have noted...I have been keeping up a full schedule every day, including weekends.
"For me, the tough weekly work schedule is part of the therapy."
